description: Canonical JSON conformance vectors shared by shared/src/crypto.ts (canonicalJson) and guest/internal/canonical (Marshal). Both suites must reproduce every expected string byte for byte.
numberPolicy: JSON numbers are IEEE-754 doubles on both sides: JS has one number type and Go decodes into float64. Encoding follows ECMAScript Number::toString(10), which is what JSON.stringify emits: shortest round-trip digits, plain notation when the decimal exponent is in -6..20, exponential form outside that range with a signed, unpadded exponent. Literals beyond 2^53 pin the double they collapse to, not the digits as written.

vectors.name: null
vectors.note: JSON null encodes as the literal null.

vectors.name: number-negative-zero
vectors.note: ECMAScript Number::toString renders -0 as 0; the encoder must never emit -0.

vectors.name: number-integral-float
vectors.note: 1.0 is the double 1, so it encodes as 1 with no fraction or exponent.

vectors.name: number-tenth
vectors.note: Shortest round-trip digits, plain notation.

vectors.name: number-repeating
vectors.note: 17 significant digits: shortest that round-trips.

vectors.name: number-1e21
vectors.note: At 1e21 ECMAScript switches to exponential form, with a signed, unpadded exponent.

vectors.name: number-1e20
vectors.note: Integral but above int64: must print 21 digits, not 1e+20.

vectors.name: number-1e6
vectors.note: Integral boundary of ECMAScript plain notation.

vectors.name: number-large-fraction
vectors.note: Fractional value with decimal exponent 6: ECMAScript stays plain, Go %g would emit 1.2345675e+06.

vectors.name: number-1e-4
vectors.note: Lower boundary of plain notation: 0.0001.

vectors.name: number-1e-5
vectors.note: ECMAScript keeps plain notation down to 1e-6; Go %g switches at 1e-5.

vectors.name: number-1e-7
vectors.note: ECMAScript exponents are not zero padded: 1e-7, not 1e-07.

vectors.name: number-max-safe-integer
vectors.note: 2^53-1, the largest integer every double holds exactly.

vectors.name: number-beyond-max-safe-integer
vectors.note: The literal is 2^53+1, which is not a double. Both sides read JSON numbers as IEEE-754 doubles, so the literal collapses to 9007199254740992 before encoding. Pinned deliberately: number handling is float64 on both sides.

vectors.name: number-thirty-digit-integer
vectors.note: Beyond int64 and beyond 2^53: reads as the nearest double and encodes in exponential form.

vectors.name: string-whitespace-escapes
vectors.note: \n, \t and \r use short escapes in both implementations.

vectors.name: string-backspace-formfeed
vectors.note: ECMAScript emits \b and \f; older Go encoders emitted \u0008 and \u000c.

vectors.name: string-control-characters
vectors.note: Other C0 controls use lowercase \u00XX hex.

vectors.name: string-del-and-c1
vectors.note: U+007F and U+0085 are escaped by neither side.

vectors.name: string-astral
vectors.note: Non-BMP characters are emitted as raw UTF-8, never as surrogate escapes.

vectors.name: string-mixed-planes
vectors.note: Astral rune between BMP runes: no surrogate pair escaping.

vectors.name: string-line-separator
vectors.note: U+2028/U+2029 are legal raw in JSON and must not be \u escaped.

vectors.name: string-html-characters
vectors.note: No HTML escaping: <, > and & stay raw.

vectors.name: keys-insertion-order-irrelevant
vectors.note: Insertion order never survives: keys sort by code unit.

vectors.name: keys-case-and-length
vectors.note: Uppercase sorts before lowercase; a prefix sorts before its extension.

vectors.name: keys-numeric-like
vectors.note: Integer-index keys are re-ordered by JS object semantics before the sort; canonical order is lexicographic, not numeric.

vectors.name: keys-astral-before-bmp
vectors.note: JS compares UTF-16 code units, so surrogate 0xD83D sorts before 0xFFFD. Go byte order sorts F0.. after EF.. and disagrees.

vectors.name: keys-astral-before-private-use
vectors.note: Same divergence against a U+E000..U+FFFF key.

vectors.name: nested-reordered-equals
vectors.note: Paired with nested-reordered-original: same content, different literal order, identical bytes.

vectors.name: attestation-envelope
vectors.note: The unsigned attestation envelope shape that canonicalEvidenceBytes hashes.

vectors.name: payment-identity
vectors.note: The paymentKey preimage shape.
